plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis 'Somei-Yoshino'
plants.description: Bare branches disappear under clouds of blush-white blossoms. Petals drift down like confetti and cover paths and canals in pink. Crowds gather beneath the trees for hanami, the centuries-old custom of picnicking under the blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April. In Kyoto, full bloom usually falls around April 4.
plants.funFact: Every Somei-Yoshino tree is a clone, grown from grafted cuttings. Neighboring trees therefore tend to open on almost the same day, which is why the bloom seems to sweep through a city all at once.

plants.name: Lupinus texensis
plants.description: Roadsides and prairies across central Texas turn into rolling blue carpets. Each spike carries pea-like flowers, and the upper petal has a small white patch that fades to magenta as the flower ages.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April, with peak bloom in early April across much of Central and East Texas.
plants.funFact: The white spot on a young bluebonnet turns reddish-purple once the flower has been pollinated. This signals to bees that it has nothing left to offer, so they move on to fresher blooms.

plants.name: Anigozanthos manglesii
plants.description: Fuzzy, velvety tubular flowers rise on tall stalks and flare open at the tip into claw-like lobes. The bright red stems and lime-green blooms look almost unreal against the sandy bush of southwestern Australia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Kangaroo paws flower from late winter into autumn. Blooms are still on show in early April, the start of the southern autumn.
plants.funFact: This is the floral emblem of Western Australia. The flowers are shaped to fit the curved beaks of honeyeater birds, which brush pollen onto their heads as they feed.
